stem: In quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(\overline{AB}\) is parallel to \(\overline{DC}\), and diagonals \(\overline{AC}\) and \(\overline{BD}\) intersect at point \(E\). If \(AB = 6\), \(DC = 15\), and \(AC = 14\), what is the length of \(\overline{AE}\)?
solution: Angles \(AEB\) and \(CED\) are vertical angles, and because \(\overline{AB} \parallel \overline{DC}\), angles \(BAE\) and \(DCE\) are alternate interior angles. So triangle \(ABE\) is similar to triangle \(CDE\).
The ratio of corresponding sides is \(\frac{AE}{CE} = \frac{AB}{CD} = \frac{6}{15}\), so \(AE\) is 6 parts and \(CE\) is 15 parts of the diagonal.
verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['A'][1]==P['B'][1] and P['C'][1]==P['D'][1] and abs(d('A','B')-6)<0.01 and abs(d('D','C')-15)<0.01 and abs(d('A','C')-14)<0.01
assert abs(ang('A','E','C')-180)<0.1 and abs(ang('B','E','D')-180)<0.1
ans=Rational(14*6,6+15)
assert abs(d('A','E')-ans)<0.01
assert Rational(spr_answers[0])==ans==4
